title: Beta Israel tradition of bringing the Ark via Elephantine
place_text: Elephantine Island, Egypt to Lake Tana, Ethiopia

tellings.quote: that their ancestors brought the Ark of the Covenant to Ethiopia
their ancestors had fled from Israel carrying the Ark. Like how they brought it to an island in the Nile River and kept it there for several hundred years.
tellings.difference: Says the Ark was kept on the Nile island for several hundred years and cites the Kebra Nagast.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell the Beta Israel tradition that their ancestors brought the Ark from Israel via a Nile island to Lake Tana, Ethiopia.

as_told.title: Falasha (Beta Israel) tradition of the Ark's journey to Ethiopia
as_told.place_text: Israel; island in the Nile; Lake Tana, Ethiopia

plain: The Beta Israel, the Jewish community of Ethiopia, hold that their ancestors fled Israel carrying the Ark of the Covenant and brought it to Ethiopia, the writer Graham Hancock tells Michels, by way of an island in the Nile, Elephantine, where they kept it, and later to Lake Tana. Hancock summarises the tradition in one conversation, and in another he says the Beta Israel (also called Falashas) told him directly that the Ark stayed on the Nile island for several hundred years. He links it to the Kebra Nagast, an old Ethiopian book; if the tradition is right, the lost Ark went south into Africa.
